outputs.name: html_report

tools.name: Cutadapt
tools.description: Removes adapter sequences and low-quality ends from reads.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Reads
inputs.description: Sequencing reads in FASTQ format (plain or .gz).

outputs.name: trimmed
outputs.label: Trimmed reads
outputs.description: Reads after adapter removal.

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: Trimming report
outputs.description: Cutadapt's summary of what it removed. MultiQC reads it.

params.label: 3' adapter sequence
params.description: Adapter to cut from the 3' end. Default: the Illumina universal adapter. D-Plex small RNA kit: AAAAAAAAAACAAAAAAAAAAGATCGGAAGAGCACACGTCTGAACTCCAGTCAC, with overlap 10.

params.label: Allowed errors in the adapter
params.description: Share of the adapter that may be mismatched, for example 0.1 allows one error in 10 bases. Cutadapt's own default is 0.1.

params.label: Minimum overlap with the adapter
params.description: Bases of the read that must match the start of the adapter before it is cut. 3 is Cutadapt's default; use 10 when the adapter starts with poly(A), so a run of A is not taken for it.

params.label: Minimum read length
params.description: Reads shorter than this after trimming are discarded.

params.label: Quality cutoff
params.description: Trim low-quality bases from the 3' end below this Phred score.

params.label: Discard reads without the adapter
params.description: Drops reads in which no adapter was found. Off keeps them: in a footprint library these are long fragments rather than footprints, which a later length filter can remove.

tools.name: BWA MEM
tools.description: Aligns reads to a reference genome. Writes SAM.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The reference FASTA the reads are aligned to. Connect BWA index to use its indexed copy, or give a FASTA you indexed yourself (the index files sit next to it).

inputs.name: reads1
inputs.label: Reads (first of the pair)
inputs.description: FASTQ with the reads, or the first file of a pair.

inputs.name: reads2
inputs.label: Reads (second of the pair)
inputs.description: Leave empty for single-end reads.

outputs.name: sam

outputs.description: The alignments in SAM format.

params.label: Mark shorter split hits as secondary
params.description: Needed by Picard and GATK.

params.label: Minimum seed length
params.description: Matches shorter than this are dropped. Smaller is more sensitive and slower.

params.label: Sample name

tools.name: Bowtie2
tools.description: Aligns reads to an indexed genome, single-end or as read pairs. Writes SAM.

inputs.name: index
inputs.label: Genome index
inputs.description: The index made with Bowtie2 build (connect it), or the prefix of one you built yourself: the path without .1.bt2 and the rest.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Reads (first of the pair)
inputs.description: FASTQ with the reads, or the first file of a pair (plain or .gz).

inputs.name: reads2
inputs.label: Reads (second of the pair)
inputs.description: Leave empty for single-end reads.

outputs.name: sam
outputs.label: Alignments
outputs.description: The alignments in SAM format.

params.label: Preset
params.description: Speed against sensitivity.

params.label: Longest fragment for pairs
params.description: Read pairs further apart than this many bases are not counted as proper pairs. Use 2000 for ATAC-seq, whose fragments can be long. Ignored for single-end reads.

tools.command: set -- -U "{reads}"; if [ -n "{reads2}" ]; then set -- -1 "{reads}" -2 "{reads2}"; fi; bowtie2 -p {threads} --{preset} -x {index} -X {max_fragment} "$@" -S {sam}

inputs.name: reads1

outputs.name: sam

outputs.description: The alignments in SAM format.

outputs.name: merged

params.description: Tick this only if the BAM files were sorted by read name. Off means sorted by genome position.

tools.name: samtools markdup
tools.description: Finds PCR duplicates and marks (or removes) them. Runs fixmate and sort first, so plain aligner output works.

inputs.name: alignments
inputs.label: Alignments
inputs.description: A SAM or BAM file with paired-end reads.

outputs.name: marked
outputs.label: Alignments with duplicates marked
outputs.description: A BAM sorted by genome position.

outputs.name: stats
outputs.label: Duplicate statistics
outputs.description: How many reads were examined and how many are duplicates.

params.label: Remove duplicates instead of marking them
params.description: Off keeps every read and only flags the duplicates.

params.description: 0 switches optical duplicate detection off. Use 100 for HiSeq-type machines or about 2500 for NovaSeq.

tools.command: set -o pipefail; samtools sort -n -@ {threads} {alignments} | samtools fixmate -m -@ {threads} - - | samtools sort -@ {threads} - | samtools markdup -@ {threads} {remove_duplicates} -d {optical_distance} -f {stats} - {marked}

tools.name: Picard MarkDuplicates
tools.description: Finds PCR duplicates in a sorted BAM and marks (or removes) them. Writes a duplication report.

outputs.name: metrics

params.label: Remove duplicates instead of marking them
params.description: Off keeps every read and only flags the duplicates.

params.label: Optical duplicate distance

params.label: Minimum base quality
params.description: Bases below this quality are not counted.

params.description: Reads below this mapping quality are not counted.

outputs.name: vcf

params.description: A variant is reported only if at least this share of the reads at its position carry it.

params.description: A variant is reported only if at least this many reads carry it.

params.label: Minimum mapping quality
params.description: Reads below this mapping quality are ignored.

params.label: Minimum base quality
params.description: Bases below this quality are ignored.

tools.name: snpEff build database
tools.description: Builds a snpEff database for your own genome from its FASTA and gene annotation (GTF).

inputs.label: Reference genome

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Gene annotation

outputs.description: Folder holding the database. Connect it to snpEff annotate.

params.description: Names the database inside the folder. Use the same name in snpEff annotate.

params.label: Memory limit
params.description: For example 2g or 8g.

tools.command: mkdir -p {database}{genome_name} && cp {genome} {database}{genome_name}/sequences.fa && cp {annotation} {database}{genome_name}/genes.gtf && cfg=$(mktemp ./.snpeff_config.XXXXXX) && printf '%s.genome : %s\n' {genome_name} {genome_name} > "$cfg" && snpEff -Xmx{memory} -Duser.language=en -Duser.country=US build -gtf22 -noCheckCds -noCheckProtein -c "$cfg" -dataDir {database} {genome_name}; status=$?; rm -f "$cfg"; exit $status

tools.description: Says what each variant does to the genes: missense, synonymous, intron, intergenic and so on.

inputs.name: vcf
inputs.label: Variants
inputs.description: A VCF file.

inputs.name: database
inputs.label: snpEff database folder
inputs.description: The folder that holds the genome's database: the output of snpEff build database, or a data folder from snpEff download.

outputs.name: annotated
outputs.label: Annotated variants
outputs.description: The VCF with an ANN field on every variant.

outputs.name: summary
outputs.label: Summary page
outputs.description: An HTML summary of the effects. MultiQC reads it.

outputs.name: stats

params.label: Upstream and downstream distance
params.description: A variant this close before or after a gene is called upstream or downstream of it.

params.label: Leave out variants between genes
params.description: Skips the intergenic variants in the output.

params.label: Memory limit
params.description: For example 2g or 8g.

tools.command: cfg=$(mktemp ./.snpeff_config.XXXXXX) && printf '%s.genome : %s\n' {genome_name} {genome_name} > "$cfg" && snpEff -Xmx{memory} -Duser.language=en -Duser.country=US ann -c "$cfg" -dataDir {database} -ud {updown_distance} {no_intergenic} -stats {summary} -csvStats {stats} {genome_name} {vcf} > {annotated}; status=$?; rm -f "$cfg"; exit $status

tools.name: Salmon index
tools.description: Builds the index Salmon quant needs from transcript sequences.

inputs.name: transcripts
inputs.label: Transcript sequences
inputs.description: One FASTA entry per transcript (cDNA). Make it from a genome and an annotation with gffread.

outputs.name: index_dir
outputs.label: Index folder
outputs.description: The Salmon index. Connect it to Salmon quant.

params.label: Word size (k-mer)
params.description: Odd number. 31 suits reads of 75 bases or longer; use about 21 for shorter reads.

tools.name: STAR genome index
tools.description: Builds the genome index STAR needs to align RNA-seq reads, with the known splice junctions of an annotation.

inputs.name: genome
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The genome FASTA to index.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Gene annotation
inputs.description: Optional but recommended: STAR then knows the splice junctions of your genes. GTF format. Required for the Ribo-seq STAR step, which writes alignments in transcript coordinates.

outputs.name: index_dir
outputs.label: Index folder
outputs.description: The STAR index. Connect it to STAR as the genome index.

params.label: Splice junction overhang
params.description: Longest read length minus 1. 100 suits reads up to 101 bases, which covers ribosome footprints (about 20 to 40 bases, up to 85 when long fragments are kept). Only used when a gene annotation is given.

params.label: Index size setting
params.description: 14 suits a human or mouse genome. For a small genome use about log2(genome size) / 2 - 1 (a 5 million base genome: 10).

tools.name: kallisto index
tools.description: Builds the index kallisto quant needs from transcript sequences.

inputs.name: transcripts
inputs.label: Transcript sequences
inputs.description: One FASTA entry per transcript (cDNA). Make it from a genome and an annotation with gffread.

outputs.name: index
outputs.label: Index file
outputs.description: The kallisto index. Connect it to kallisto quant.

params.label: Word size (k-mer)
params.description: Odd number up to 31. Use a smaller value (about 21) for reads shorter than 50 bases.

tools.name: gffread transcripts
tools.description: Cuts the transcript sequences (exons joined together) out of a genome using an annotation.

inputs.name: genome
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The genome FASTA the annotation belongs to. gffread also writes a .fai index file next to it.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Gene annotation
inputs.description: Gene annotation in GTF or GFF3 format.

outputs.name: transcripts
outputs.label: Transcript sequences
outputs.description: One FASTA entry per transcript. Connect it to Salmon index or kallisto index.

tools.name: Annotation to BED12
tools.description: Converts a gene annotation (GTF or GFF3) to the BED12 gene model that RSeQC reads.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Gene annotation
inputs.description: Gene annotation in GTF or GFF3 format.

outputs.name: bed
outputs.label: Gene model (BED12)
outputs.description: One line per transcript with its exon blocks. Connect it to the RSeQC steps.

tools.name: HISAT2
tools.description: Splice-aware RNA-seq aligner, single-end or paired-end. Writes SAM.

inputs.name: index
inputs.label: Genome index folder
inputs.description: The folder made with HISAT2 build (connect it).

inputs.name: reads1
inputs.label: Reads (first of the pair)
inputs.description: FASTQ with the reads, or the first file of a pair.

inputs.name: reads2
inputs.label: Reads (second of the pair)
inputs.description: Leave empty for single-end reads.

outputs.name: sam
outputs.label: Alignments
outputs.description: The alignments in SAM format. Sort them with samtools sort next.

outputs.name: summary
outputs.label: Alignment summary
outputs.description: How many reads aligned. MultiQC reads it.

params.label: Prepare for StringTie
params.description: Tick this when the alignments go to StringTie to assemble transcripts.

params.label: Longest intron
params.description: Introns longer than this many bases are not searched for. The default suits most animals; lower it for yeast or plants.

tools.command: set -- -U {reads1}; if [ -n "{reads2}" ]; then set -- -1 {reads1} -2 {reads2}; fi; hisat2 -p {threads} {dta} --max-intronlen {max_intron} -x {index}/genome "$@" -S {sam} --new-summary --summary-file {summary}

tools.name: kallisto quant
tools.description: Quantifies transcript abundance from single-end or paired-end reads, without aligning them.

inputs.name: index
inputs.label: kallisto index
inputs.description: The index made with kallisto index (connect it).

inputs.name: reads1
inputs.label: Reads (first of the pair)
inputs.description: FASTQ with the reads, or the first file of a pair.

inputs.name: reads2
inputs.label: Reads (second of the pair)
inputs.description: Leave empty for single-end reads. kallisto then needs the fragment length from Options.

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Result folder
outputs.description: kallisto writes its results here.

outputs.name: abundance
outputs.label: Abundances
outputs.description: The table of transcript abundances. It is always called abundance.tsv inside the result folder.

outputs.name: log
outputs.label: Run log
outputs.description: kallisto's progress messages. MultiQC reads it.

params.label: Average fragment length
params.description: Only used for single-end reads (when the second reads file is empty): the average length of the sequenced DNA fragments, from your library preparation.

params.label: Fragment length spread
params.description: Only used for single-end reads: the standard deviation of the fragment length.

params.label: Library strandedness
params.description: Pick what your library kit makes. Most Illumina kits (TruSeq stranded, dUTP) are reverse-stranded. If unsure, run RSeQC infer experiment on an alignment.

option_labels.--rf-stranded: Reverse-stranded (dUTP kits: read 1 is the opposite strand)

params.label: Bootstrap samples
params.description: Repeats of the estimate that show how certain it is. Needed only to compare samples with sleuth; 0 is fastest.

tools.command: set -- --single -l {fragment_length} -s {fragment_sd}; if [ -n "{reads2}" ]; then set --; fi; kallisto quant -i {index} -o {out_dir} -t {threads} "$@" {strand} -b {bootstrap_samples} {reads1} {reads2} 2> {log} || (cat {log} >&2; false)

tools.name: StringTie assemble
tools.description: Assembles transcripts from RNA-seq alignments, optionally guided by a gene annotation, and estimates their abundance.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM sorted by genome position. Made with HISAT2 (tick Prepare for StringTie) and samtools sort.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Guide annotation
inputs.description: Optional. With an annotation StringTie also finds the known genes; without one it assembles from the reads alone.

outputs.name: gtf
outputs.label: Assembled transcripts
outputs.description: The transcripts StringTie found, with their coverage and TPM. GTF format.

outputs.name: genes
outputs.label: Gene abundances
outputs.description: One row per gene with coverage, FPKM and TPM.

params.label: Library strandedness
params.description: Pick what your library kit makes. Most Illumina kits (TruSeq stranded, dUTP) are reverse-stranded. If unsure, run RSeQC infer experiment on an alignment.

option_labels.--rf: Reverse-stranded (dUTP kits: read 1 is the opposite strand)

params.label: Minimum coverage
params.description: Transcripts covered by fewer reads on average than this are dropped.

params.label: Minimum isoform fraction
params.description: Transcripts of a gene with less than this share of the gene's reads are dropped (0 to 1).

tools.name: StringTie quantify
tools.description: Measures the abundance of the transcripts of an annotation (no new transcripts are made).

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM sorted by genome position.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Gene annotation
inputs.description: The transcripts to measure: a GTF or GFF3 file, or the assembled transcripts of StringTie assemble.

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Result folder
outputs.description: StringTie writes its tables here, including the .ctab files Ballgown reads.

outputs.name: transcripts
outputs.label: Transcript abundances
outputs.description: The annotated transcripts with coverage, FPKM and TPM. Always called transcripts.gtf inside the result folder.

outputs.name: genes
outputs.label: Gene abundances
outputs.description: One row per gene. Always called gene_abundances.tsv inside the result folder.

params.label: Library strandedness
params.description: Pick what your library kit makes. Most Illumina kits (TruSeq stranded, dUTP) are reverse-stranded. If unsure, run RSeQC infer experiment on an alignment.

option_labels.--rf: Reverse-stranded (dUTP kits: read 1 is the opposite strand)

tools.name: RSeQC infer experiment
tools.description: Works out whether an RNA-seq library is stranded, and which way, from where reads fall on genes.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM of RNA-seq reads aligned to the genome.

inputs.name: gene_model
inputs.label: Gene model (BED12)
inputs.description: The genes in BED12 format. Make it from a GTF with Annotation to BED12.

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: Strandedness report
outputs.description: The share of reads that follow each strand rule. MultiQC reads it.

params.label: Reads to check
params.description: The first this many reads that fall on genes are checked. More is slower and barely changes the answer.

params.label: Minimum mapping quality
params.description: Reads below this mapping quality are skipped.

tools.name: RSeQC read distribution
tools.description: Shows how the reads divide between exons, introns and the regions around genes.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM of RNA-seq reads aligned to the genome.

inputs.name: gene_model
inputs.label: Gene model (BED12)
inputs.description: The genes in BED12 format. Make it from a GTF with Annotation to BED12.

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: Distribution report
outputs.description: Bases and read tags per region type. MultiQC reads it.

tools.name: MACS3 callpeak
tools.description: Finds the places in the genome where a ChIP-seq (or ATAC-seq) sample has more reads than expected, with an optional input control. Makes sharp peaks, summits and a signal track.

inputs.name: treatment
inputs.label: ChIP alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: The BAM of the ChIP sample, sorted by genome position. To pool replicates, merge them first with samtools merge.

inputs.name: control
inputs.label: Control alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: Optional. The input or IgG control BAM. Without a control MACS3 uses the local background of the ChIP itself, which finds more false peaks.

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Peak folder
outputs.description: Folder for the peaks and the signal track.

outputs.name: peaks
outputs.label: Peaks
outputs.description: The peaks, one per line (narrowPeak format: BED with the fold enrichment and significance of each).

outputs.name: summits
outputs.label: Summits
outputs.description: The single highest base of each peak (BED).

outputs.name: table
outputs.label: Peak table
outputs.description: The same peaks as a table with a header that describes every column (tab-separated).

outputs.name: signal
outputs.label: Signal track
outputs.description: How many fragments cover each stretch of the genome (bedGraph).

params.label: Read type
params.description: Paired-end data gives MACS3 the real size of every DNA fragment. Pick single-end if your reads have no mate.

params.label: Genome size
params.description: hs for human, mm for mouse, ce for worm, dm for fly, or the size of your genome in bases, for example 4600000. MACS3 uses it to estimate the background.

params.label: Significance cut-off (q-value)
params.description: A peak must be at least this significant after correcting for the number of places tested. Smaller keeps fewer, more certain peaks.

params.label: Fragment length (single-end only)
params.description: Single-end only: every read is extended to this length, the size of the DNA pieces you sequenced. Paired-end data ignores it.

params.label: Duplicate reads
params.description: Several reads that start at exactly the same place are often PCR copies.

option_labels.1: Keep one read per position (drops PCR copies)
option_labels.auto: Let MACS3 decide from the data

params.label: Split touching peaks at their summits
params.description: Tick this when neighbouring binding sites are merged into one wide peak. Each summit then becomes its own peak.

tools.command: C="{control}"; E=""; if [ {format} = BAM ]; then E="--nomodel --extsize {fragment_length}"; fi; macs3 callpeak -t {treatment} ${C:+-c "$C"} -f {format} -g {genome_size} -q {qvalue} --keep-dup {keep_dup} $E {call_summits} -B -n sample --outdir {out_dir}

tools.name: Genrich
tools.description: Finds open chromatin in ATAC-seq data (or enriched regions in ChIP-seq). It reads all replicates together and takes the Tn5 cut sites into account.

inputs.name: alignments
inputs.label: Alignments sorted by read name (BAM)
inputs.description: Genrich needs BAM files sorted by read NAME, not by position: use samtools sort and tick Sort by read name. Connect several steps to call peaks from all replicates together. File names must not contain commas.

inputs.name: control
inputs.label: Control alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: Optional. A control sample, also sorted by read name.

inputs.name: blacklist
inputs.label: Regions to ignore
inputs.description: Optional. A BED file of regions that should never become peaks, such as known artefact regions.

outputs.name: peaks
outputs.label: Peaks
outputs.description: The peaks in narrowPeak format (BED with a significance for each).

params.label: ATAC-seq mode
params.description: Counts where the transposase cut the DNA instead of whole reads. Untick it for ChIP-seq alignments.

params.label: Significance cut-off (q-value)
params.description: A peak must be at least this significant after correcting for the number of places tested. Smaller keeps fewer, more certain peaks.

params.label: Minimum peak strength
params.description: Peaks with less total signal than this are dropped. Raise it for fewer, stronger peaks.

params.label: Minimum peak length (bases)
params.description: Shorter peaks are dropped.

params.label: Join peaks closer than (bases)
params.description: Two peaks separated by less than this become one.

params.label: Minimum mapping quality
params.description: Reads that map with less confidence than this are ignored.

params.label: Remove PCR duplicates
params.description: Reads that are exact copies of each other are counted once.

params.label: Chromosomes to ignore
params.description: Names separated by commas, for example chrM,chrY. Mitochondrial DNA is open in every ATAC-seq sample and would hide real peaks. Leave empty to use every chromosome.

tools.name: deepTools bamCoverage
tools.description: Turns alignments into a signal track (bigWig) that shows how many reads cover each stretch of the genome, scaled so that samples can be compared.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM sorted by genome position.

inputs.name: bai
inputs.label: BAM index
inputs.description: The .bai file of this BAM (make it with samtools index). It must sit next to the BAM and be named like it, ending in .bam.bai.

inputs.name: blacklist
inputs.label: Regions to leave out
inputs.description: Optional. A BED file of regions that should have no signal.

outputs.name: coverage
outputs.label: Signal track
outputs.description: The signal in bigWig format. Load it in a genome browser or give it to computeMatrix.

params.label: Scale the signal
params.description: Scaling makes samples with different numbers of reads comparable.

params.label: Bin size (bases)
params.description: The signal is averaged in bins of this size. Smaller bins are sharper and make bigger files.

params.label: Read length used
params.description: Paired-end data only. Extending covers the whole DNA fragment between the two reads, which is what you want for ChIP-seq. Leave it as sequenced for single-end data.

option_labels.--extendReads: Paired-end: cover the whole fragment between the two reads

params.label: Minimum mapping quality
params.description: Reads that map with less confidence than this are not counted.

params.label: Count duplicate reads once
params.description: Reads with the same start and direction are counted only once.

tools.name: deepTools computeMatrix
tools.description: Collects the signal around one point of every region (the centre of each peak, or the start of each gene) into a table. plotHeatmap draws it.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.label: Signal tracks (bigWig)
inputs.description: One or more tracks from bamCoverage. Connect several steps to compare samples in one picture.

inputs.name: regions
inputs.label: Regions
inputs.description: The regions to look around, for example peaks or genes. Each file becomes its own group in the heatmap.

outputs.name: matrix
outputs.label: Signal matrix
outputs.description: The collected signal, ready for plotHeatmap.

outputs.name: sorted_regions
outputs.label: Regions in matrix order
outputs.description: The regions as they appear in the matrix (BED). Regions with no signal may have been skipped.

outputs.name: values
outputs.label: Matrix as a table
outputs.description: The same numbers as plain text: one row per region, one column per bin (tab-separated).

params.label: Look around
params.description: The point of each region that the signal is centred on.

option_labels.TSS: The start of each region (the transcription start of a gene)

params.label: Distance before the point (bases)
params.description: How far to look in front of the point.

params.label: Distance after the point (bases)
params.description: How far to look behind the point.

params.label: Bin size (bases)
params.description: The signal is averaged in bins of this size. It should be at least the bin size of the tracks.

params.label: Leave out regions with no signal
params.description: Regions that have no signal in any track are not put in the matrix.

params.label: Count missing data as zero
params.description: Regions that run past the end of a chromosome, or have no data, count as zero instead of leaving gaps.

tools.name: deepTools plotHeatmap
tools.description: Draws a heatmap of the signal around your regions, one row per region, with an average profile on top.

inputs.name: matrix
inputs.label: Signal matrix
inputs.description: The matrix made by computeMatrix.

outputs.name: heatmap
outputs.label: Heatmap
outputs.description: The picture. The ending of the name sets the format: .png, .pdf or .svg.

params.label: Colour scheme
params.description: The colours of the signal, from low to high.

option_labels.viridis: Purple to yellow (easy to read in black and white)
option_labels.RdBu_r: Blue to red (for values above and below zero)

params.label: Order of the rows
params.description: How the regions are ordered from top to bottom.

params.label: Measure the signal by
params.description: Which number of each region decides its place when the rows are ordered by signal.

params.label: Title
params.description: Optional text above the picture.

params.label: Resolution (dots per inch)
params.description: Higher is sharper and makes a bigger file. 200 is fine for slides, 300 for print.

tools.name: deepTools plotFingerprint
tools.description: Shows how well a ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq sample is enriched: a good ChIP puts most of its reads into a small part of the genome, an input control spreads them evenly.

inputs.name: bams
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: The samples to compare, usually the ChIP and its input control. Sorted by genome position.

inputs.name: bais
inputs.label: BAM indexes
inputs.description: The .bai file of every BAM above (make them with samtools index). Each must sit next to its BAM and be named like it, ending in .bam.bai.

outputs.name: plot
outputs.label: Fingerprint plot
outputs.description: The picture: one curve per sample. The ending of the name sets the format: .png, .pdf or .svg.

outputs.name: metrics
outputs.label: Quality numbers
outputs.description: The numbers behind the curves, one row per sample (tab-separated).

params.label: Places to count
params.description: How many places in the genome are sampled. Use a few hundred for a very small genome.

params.label: Bin size (bases)
params.description: Each place is this many bases wide.

params.label: Read length used
params.description: Paired-end data only. Extending covers the whole DNA fragment between the two reads, which is what you want for ChIP-seq. Leave it as sequenced for single-end data.

option_labels.--extendReads: Paired-end: cover the whole fragment between the two reads

params.label: Leave out empty places
params.description: Places where no sample has reads are not counted.

tools.command: for f in {bais}; do test -s "$f" || { echo "missing BAM index: $f" >&2; exit 1; }; done; MPLBACKEND=Agg plotFingerprint -b {bams} -plot {plot} --outQualityMetrics {metrics} --numberOfProcessors {threads} --numberOfSamples {sample_regions} --binSize {bin_size} {extend} {skip_zeros}

tools.name: bedtools intersect
tools.description: Compares two sets of regions: keeps the ones that overlap, the ones that do not, or just the overlapping stretches. For example, which peaks of one sample are also peaks in another.

inputs.name: a
inputs.label: Regions to check (A)
inputs.description: The regions you want to keep or drop, for example your peaks.

inputs.name: b
inputs.label: Regions to compare with (B)
inputs.description: The regions A is compared with, for example the peaks of another sample or the promoters of your genes.

outputs.name: result
outputs.label: Result
outputs.description: The regions that were kept, in the same format as A.

params.label: What to report
params.description: Which regions end up in the result.

option_labels.-u: Each A region that overlaps B
option_labels: Only the overlapping stretch of each A region
option_labels.-v: Each A region that does NOT overlap B
option_labels.-c: Every A region, with the number of B regions it overlaps added
option_labels.-wa -wb: Each overlapping pair, A and B side by side

params.label: Minimum overlap
params.description: Leave empty to count any overlap of at least one base. Or enter a fraction of A between 0 and 1: 0.5 means at least half of the A region must be covered.

params.label: The overlap must be just as large for B
params.description: With a minimum overlap, B must be covered by that fraction as well, not only A.

params.label: Strand
params.description: Whether the direction of the regions matters.

tools.name: bedtools merge
tools.description: Joins regions that overlap (or lie close together) into single regions. Give it the peaks of several samples to get one combined set.

inputs.name: intervals
inputs.label: Regions
inputs.description: Peaks or other regions. Connect several steps to combine samples. They do not need to be sorted.

outputs.name: merged
outputs.label: Merged regions
outputs.description: One line per joined region: chromosome, start and end (BED).

params.label: Join regions closer than (bases)
params.description: 0 joins only regions that overlap or touch. 100 also joins regions up to 100 bases apart.

params.label: Add how many regions were joined
params.description: Adds a column with the number of regions that make up each merged region.

tools.command: awk 'BEGIN{FS=OFS="\t"} !/^(#|track|browser)/ && NF>=3 {print $1,$2,$3}' {intervals} | LC_ALL=C sort -k1,1 -k2,2n | bedtools merge -i - -d {distance} {count} > {merged}

tools.name: bedtools genomecov
tools.description: Measures how deeply every stretch of the genome is covered by reads and writes it as a bedGraph track.

inputs.name: bam
inputs.label: Alignments (BAM)
inputs.description: A BAM sorted by genome position.

outputs.name: coverage
outputs.label: Coverage track
outputs.description: Chromosome, start, end and depth of each stretch (bedGraph).

params.label: Stretches to write
params.description: Whether stretches with no reads are written.

option_labels.-bga: Every stretch, including those with no reads

params.label: Count paired reads as whole fragments
params.description: Paired-end only: the whole stretch between the two reads counts as covered, not just the reads themselves.

params.label: Do not count gaps inside reads
params.description: For RNA-seq: spliced reads cover their exons, not the introns they skip.

params.label: Multiply the depth by
params.description: 1 gives raw read depth. For reads per million, use 1000000 divided by the number of reads in the BAM.

tools.name: bedtools getfasta
tools.description: Cuts the DNA sequence of every region out of a genome FASTA, for example the sequences under your peaks for a motif search.

inputs.name: genome
inputs.label: Genome sequence (FASTA)
inputs.description: The genome the regions refer to. bedtools writes a .fai index next to it the first time; connect the Indexed reference of samtools faidx to keep your own folder clean.

inputs.name: regions
inputs.label: Regions
inputs.description: The regions to cut out, for example peaks.

outputs.name: sequences
outputs.label: Sequences
outputs.description: One sequence per region (FASTA).

params.label: Name each sequence by
params.description: What is written in the header line of every sequence.

option_labels.-nameOnly: The name column of the region file

params.label: Reverse-complement regions on the minus strand
params.description: Reads each region in the direction of its gene or feature. Needs a region file with a strand column.

tools.name: HOMER annotatePeaks
tools.description: Tells you where each peak lies: in a promoter, an exon, an intron or between genes, and which gene is closest. Uses the genome FASTA and gene annotation you connect.

inputs.name: peaks
inputs.label: Peaks
inputs.description: The regions to annotate (BED or narrowPeak).

inputs.name: genome
inputs.label: Genome sequence (FASTA)
inputs.description: The genome the peaks refer to.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Gene annotation
inputs.description: A GTF file of the genes of this genome.

outputs.name: annotated
outputs.label: Annotated peaks
outputs.description: One row per peak: position, the kind of place it lies in, the distance to the nearest gene start and that gene (tab-separated).

outputs.name: stats
outputs.label: Summary by place
outputs.description: How many peaks lie in promoters, exons, introns and other places, compared with what chance would give.

params.label: Region size
params.description: given uses every peak as it is. A number such as 200 looks at that many bases around the centre of each peak instead.

needs_database.label: Genome FASTA and gene annotation
needs_database.hint: Connect your genome FASTA and a GTF with the same chromosome names. Nothing is downloaded.

tools.name: minimap2 (long reads)
tools.description: Aligns long reads (Nanopore, PacBio HiFi or cDNA) to a reference genome. Pick the preset that matches how the reads were made. Writes SAM.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: The genome FASTA the reads are aligned to. No index is needed.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Long reads
inputs.description: FASTQ or FASTA with the long reads. Compressed files (.gz) work.

outputs.name: sam
outputs.label: Alignments
outputs.description: The alignments in SAM format. Sort and index them with samtools next.

params.label: Kind of reads
params.description: Tells minimap2 how many errors to expect. Use the spliced presets for cDNA or RNA reads, which are cut across introns.

option_labels.lr:hq: Nanopore DNA reads, newest chemistry (Q20 and better)
option_labels.splice: Nanopore cDNA or direct RNA reads, spliced
option_labels.splice:hq: Accurate cDNA reads such as Iso-Seq, spliced

params.label: Sample name
params.description: Optional. Written into every alignment as its read group. For example patient1.

params.label: Report only the best alignment of each read
params.description: Leaves out the second-best places a read could go. Recommended for most uses.

tools.name: NanoPlot
tools.description: Summarises a Nanopore or PacBio run: how many reads, how long and how accurate, with plots. Reads FASTQ, a Dorado BAM or a sequencing summary.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Reads or summary
inputs.description: FASTQ reads, a BAM from Dorado (unaligned or aligned), or a sequencing summary table. Pick the matching kind in Options.

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Report folder
outputs.description: Folder for the report, the statistics and the plots.

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: Report page
outputs.description: The summary page with all plots (HTML).

outputs.name: stats
outputs.label: Statistics
outputs.description: The numbers behind the report: read count, lengths, quality, N50 (text).

params.label: Kind of input
params.description: What the input file holds.

params.label: Hide reads shorter than (bases)
params.description: Reads shorter than this are left out of the plots. 0 keeps every read.

params.label: Hide reads with average quality below
params.description: Reads below this average quality score are left out of the plots. 0 keeps every read. Q10 means 1 error in 10 bases.

params.label: Plot files
params.description: The report page always has interactive plots. Picture files take a little longer.

params.label: Title
params.description: Optional. Written on every plot. For example Run 12.

tools.command: E=""; if [ {min_length} -gt 0 ]; then E="$E --minlength {min_length}"; fi; if [ {min_quality} -gt 0 ]; then E="$E --minqual {min_quality}"; fi; T={title}; NanoPlot {format} {reads} -o {out_dir} --threads {threads} --N50 {plot_files} $E ${T:+--title "$T"}

tools.name: Filtlong
tools.description: Keeps the best long reads of a Nanopore or PacBio run: drops reads that are too short or too inaccurate, and can keep only as many bases as you need. Writes a compressed FASTQ.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Long reads
inputs.description: The FASTQ file to filter. Compressed files (.gz) work.

inputs.name: short1
inputs.label: Short reads (first file)
inputs.description: Optional. Accurate short reads of the same sample. Filtlong then judges each long read by how well its pieces match them.

inputs.name: short2
inputs.label: Short reads (second file)
inputs.description: Optional. The second file of the short read pair.

outputs.name: filtered
outputs.label: Filtered reads
outputs.description: The reads that passed, as compressed FASTQ.

params.label: Shortest read to keep (bases)
params.description: Shorter reads are dropped. Long reads are what make assemblies join up, so very short ones help little.

params.label: Lowest average accuracy to keep (percent)
params.description: A read whose average accuracy is below this is dropped. 90 percent is about Q10. 0 turns the check off.

params.label: Share of the best reads to keep (percent)
params.description: Keeps only this share of the bases, best reads first. 100 keeps everything that passed the other limits.

params.label: Most bases to keep
params.description: Optional. Stop after this many bases, best reads first. For example 500m for 500 million. Useful to cap the coverage before an assembly.

params.label: Longest read to keep (bases)
params.description: Longer reads are dropped. 0 sets no limit.

tools.command: set -o pipefail; R1="{short1}"; R2="{short2}"; E=""; if [ {min_length} -gt 0 ]; then E="$E --min_length {min_length}"; fi; if [ {max_length} -gt 0 ]; then E="$E --max_length {max_length}"; fi; if [ {min_accuracy} -gt 0 ]; then E="$E --min_mean_q {min_accuracy}"; fi; if [ {keep_percent} -lt 100 ]; then E="$E --keep_percent {keep_percent}"; fi; T={target_bases}; filtlong $E ${T:+--target_bases "$T"} ${R1:+-1 "$R1"} ${R2:+-2 "$R2"} {reads} | gzip > {filtered}

tools.name: chopper
tools.description: Filters and trims long reads by their average quality and length. Fast, and the usual first step for Nanopore reads. Writes a compressed FASTQ.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Long reads
inputs.description: The FASTQ file to filter. Compressed files (.gz) work.

outputs.name: filtered
outputs.label: Filtered reads
outputs.description: The reads that passed, as compressed FASTQ.

params.label: Lowest average quality to keep
params.description: A read whose average quality score is below this is dropped. Q10 means 1 error in 10 bases. 0 turns the check off.

params.label: Shortest read to keep (bases)
params.description: Shorter reads are dropped.

params.label: Longest read to keep (bases)
params.description: Longer reads are dropped. 0 sets no limit.

params.label: Cut this many bases off the start
params.description: Removes the first bases of every read, where quality is often poor. 0 cuts nothing.

params.label: Cut this many bases off the end
params.description: Removes the last bases of every read. 0 cuts nothing.

tools.command: set -o pipefail; E=""; if [ {max_length} -gt 0 ]; then E="--maxlength {max_length}"; fi; if [ {head_crop} -gt 0 ] || [ {tail_crop} -gt 0 ]; then E="$E --trim-approach fixed-crop --headcrop {head_crop} --tailcrop {tail_crop}"; fi; chopper -i {reads} -q {min_quality} -l {min_length} --threads {threads} $E | gzip > {filtered}

tools.name: Flye
tools.description: Assembles a genome from long reads (Nanopore or PacBio) without a reference. Writes the contigs, the assembly graph and a table of contig lengths and coverage.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Long reads
inputs.description: One or more FASTQ or FASTA files from the same sample. About 30 times the genome size in bases is a good amount. Filter them first for best results.

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Assembly folder
outputs.description: Folder for the assembly and its intermediate results.

outputs.name: assembly
outputs.label: Assembled contigs
outputs.description: The assembled sequences (FASTA).

outputs.name: graph
outputs.label: Assembly graph
outputs.description: How the contigs connect (GFA). Open it in Bandage to look at it.

outputs.name: info
outputs.label: Contig table
outputs.description: One line per contig: length, coverage and whether it is circular (tab-separated).

outputs.name: log
outputs.label: Log
outputs.description: What Flye did, step by step (text).

params.label: Kind of reads
params.description: Tells Flye how many errors to expect in the reads.

option_labels.--nano-hq: Nanopore reads, newest chemistry (Q20 and better)

params.label: Expected genome size
params.description: Optional. For example 5m for 5 million bases, or 25k. Helps when the coverage is low. Leave empty to let Flye work it out.

params.label: Polishing rounds
params.description: How many times the contigs are corrected with the reads. More rounds are slower and rarely help after 2.

params.label: The sample is a mix of organisms (metagenome)
params.description: Tick this for a metagenome so Flye expects uneven coverage.

params.label: Smallest overlap between reads
params.description: Optional. In bases, for example 3000. Flye picks it from the read lengths when empty.

tools.name: SPAdes
tools.description: Assembles a genome from short Illumina reads without a reference. Writes the contigs, the scaffolds and the assembly graph.

inputs.name: reads1
inputs.label: Reads (first of the pair)
inputs.description: FASTQ with the reads, or the first file of a pair.

inputs.name: reads2
inputs.label: Reads (second of the pair)
inputs.description: Leave empty for single-end reads.

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Assembly folder
outputs.description: Folder for the assembly and its intermediate results.

outputs.name: contigs
outputs.label: Contigs
outputs.description: The assembled sequences (FASTA).

outputs.name: scaffolds
outputs.label: Scaffolds
outputs.description: Contigs joined into longer sequences where the read pairs allow it (FASTA).

outputs.name: graph
outputs.label: Assembly graph
outputs.description: How the contigs connect (GFA). Open it in Bandage to look at it.

outputs.name: log
outputs.label: Log
outputs.description: What SPAdes did, step by step (text).

params.label: Kind of sample
params.description: Picks the settings that suit the sample. A single cultured organism with plenty of reads is the usual case.

option_labels.--meta: Mix of organisms (metagenome, needs paired reads)

params.label: Memory limit (GB)
params.description: SPAdes stops if it needs more than this. Leave at 8 for small genomes; large genomes need more.

params.label: Word sizes (k-mers)
params.description: Optional. Odd numbers separated by commas, for example 21,33,55. SPAdes chooses them from the read length when empty.

tools.command: K={kmers}; set -- -s "{reads1}"; if [ -n "{reads2}" ]; then set -- -1 "{reads1}" -2 "{reads2}"; fi; spades.py {mode} -o {out_dir} -t {threads} -m {memory} ${K:+-k "$K"} "$@"

tools.name: QUAST
tools.description: Judges genome assemblies: how many contigs, how long, and (with a reference) how complete and correct. Several assemblies go into one comparison.

inputs.name: assemblies
inputs.label: Assemblies
inputs.description: One or more assembled sequences (FASTA). Give several to compare them side by side.

inputs.name: reference
inputs.label: Reference genome
inputs.description: Optional. A known genome of the same organism. With it QUAST also reports how much of it was recovered and the errors against it.

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Report folder
outputs.description: Folder for the comparison tables and the report page.

outputs.name: table
outputs.label: Comparison table
outputs.description: One column per assembly, one row per number (tab-separated).

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: Report page
outputs.description: The same numbers with plots (HTML).

outputs.name: summary
outputs.label: Text summary
outputs.description: The comparison as plain text.

params.label: Ignore contigs shorter than (bases)
params.description: Short contigs are usually noise and are left out of the numbers.

params.label: Names of the assemblies
params.description: Optional. Comma-separated, in the same order as the files. For example flye,spades. Without it the file names are used.

params.label: Contig browser
params.description: A page for scrolling along the contigs. It adds about 20 seconds.

tools.name: seqkit stats
tools.description: Counts the sequences in FASTA or FASTQ files and reports their total length, shortest, longest, N50 and average quality, one line per file.

inputs.name: sequences
inputs.label: Sequences
inputs.description: One or more FASTA or FASTQ files. Compressed files (.gz) work.

outputs.name: stats
outputs.label: Statistics table
outputs.description: One line per file (tab-separated).

params.label: Add N50 and quality statistics
params.description: Also reports N50, the share of bases above Q20 and Q30, the average quality and the GC content.

tools.name: seqkit seq (filter or convert)
tools.description: Keeps the sequences within a length or quality range, and can reverse-complement or upper-case them. Writes a compressed file.

inputs.name: sequences
inputs.label: Sequences
inputs.description: A FASTA or FASTQ file. Compressed files (.gz) work.

outputs.name: result
outputs.label: Result
outputs.description: The sequences that passed, in the same format as the input. A name ending in .gz is compressed.

params.label: Shortest sequence to keep (bases)
params.description: Shorter sequences are dropped. 0 keeps every length.

params.label: Longest sequence to keep (bases)
params.description: Longer sequences are dropped. 0 sets no limit.

params.label: Lowest average quality to keep
params.description: FASTQ only. Reads with a lower average quality score are dropped. 0 keeps every read.

params.label: Reverse-complement every sequence
params.description: Writes the other strand of every sequence.

params.label: Write sequences in upper case
params.description: Turns lower-case (soft-masked) bases into capitals.

tools.command: E=""; if [ {min_length} -gt 0 ]; then E="$E --min-len {min_length}"; fi; if [ {max_length} -gt 0 ]; then E="$E --max-len {max_length}"; fi; if [ {min_quality} -gt 0 ]; then E="$E --min-qual {min_quality}"; fi; seqkit seq -j {threads} $E {reverse_complement} {upper_case} {sequences} -o {result}

tools.name: seqkit grep (pick sequences)
tools.description: Picks sequences by name or by a stretch of sequence, from a list of names or a pattern you type. Can also leave those out instead.

inputs.name: sequences
inputs.label: Sequences
inputs.description: A FASTA or FASTQ file. Compressed files (.gz) work.

inputs.name: names
inputs.label: List of names or patterns
inputs.description: Optional. A text file with one name or pattern per line. Use it, the box in Options, or both.

outputs.name: matched
outputs.label: Picked sequences
outputs.description: The sequences that matched, in the same format as the input. A name ending in .gz is compressed.

params.label: Name or pattern
params.description: Optional. A name typed here instead of (or as well as) a list. It must match the whole name unless you tick the regular expression box. For example read_17.

params.label: Look in
params.description: Where to look for the pattern.

option_labels: The sequence name up to the first space (its ID)

params.label: Keep everything except the matches
params.description: Drops the sequences that match and keeps the rest.

params.label: Ignore capital letters
params.description: Treats A and a as the same.

params.label: The pattern is a regular expression
params.description: Tick this to write a pattern like read_1[0-9]. Leave it unticked to match the text exactly.

tools.command: P={pattern}; L="{names}"; if [ -z "$P" ] && [ -z "$L" ]; then echo "Type a name or pattern, or connect a list of names." >&2; exit 1; fi; seqkit grep -j {threads} {search_in} {invert} {ignore_case} {regex} ${P:+-p "$P"} ${L:+-f "$L"} {sequences} -o {matched}

tools.name: Kraken2 build database
tools.description: Builds a Kraken2 database from your own genomes, for example the few species you expect in a sample. Needs a taxonomy that names every genome.

inputs.name: genomes
inputs.label: Genomes
inputs.description: FASTA files. Every sequence name must carry its taxonomy number, like >seq1|kraken:taxid|562.

inputs.name: names
inputs.label: Taxonomy names
inputs.description: The names.dmp file of an NCBI-style taxonomy, listing the name of every taxonomy number.

inputs.name: nodes
inputs.label: Taxonomy tree
inputs.description: The nodes.dmp file of the same taxonomy, giving the parent and rank of every taxonomy number.

outputs.name: db
outputs.label: Database folder
outputs.description: The finished Kraken2 database. Connect it to Kraken2.

params.label: Word size (k-mer length)
params.description: Kraken2 matches reads to the genomes in words of this many bases. The standard is 35.

params.label: Minimizer length
params.description: The part of each word Kraken2 indexes. It must be at most the word size. The standard is 31.

params.label: Minimizer spaces
params.description: Positions skipped inside the minimizer to tolerate mismatches. The standard is 7.

tools.command: set -e; D="{db}"; rm -rf "$D/library" "$D/seqid2taxid.map"; mkdir -p "$D/taxonomy"; cp "{names}" "$D/taxonomy/names.dmp"; cp "{nodes}" "$D/taxonomy/nodes.dmp"; for g in {genomes}; do kraken2-build --add-to-library "$g" --db "$D"; done; kraken2-build --build --db "$D" --threads {threads} --kmer-len {kmer_length} --minimizer-len {minimizer_length} --minimizer-spaces {minimizer_spaces}

tools.name: Kraken2
tools.description: Names the organism each read most likely comes from (its taxonomy) by matching it against a database of genomes. Writes a summary table by species and a line for every read.

inputs.name: reads1
inputs.label: Reads (first of the pair)
inputs.description: FASTQ or FASTA with the reads, or the first file of a pair.

inputs.name: reads2
inputs.label: Reads (second of the pair)
inputs.description: Leave empty for single-end reads.

inputs.name: db
inputs.label: Database folder
inputs.description: A Kraken2 database: a folder you built with Kraken2 build database, or a ready-made one downloaded from the Kraken2 index page.

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: Summary by species
outputs.description: How many reads fell in each group of the tree of life, as a table (tab-separated). Bracken reads it.

outputs.name: assignments
outputs.label: Assignment of every read
outputs.description: One line per read: classified or not, which group, and how long it is (tab-separated).

params.label: Confidence needed
params.description: Share of a read that must match its group, from 0 to 1. Higher is stricter: fewer reads are named, with fewer mistakes.

params.label: Smallest number of matching words
params.description: A read needs at least this many separate matching stretches to be named.

params.label: Read the database from disk instead of memory
params.description: Tick this when the database is bigger than the free memory. It is slower.

tools.command: set -- "{reads1}"; if [ -n "{reads2}" ]; then set -- --paired "{reads1}" "{reads2}"; fi; kraken2 --db {db} --threads {threads} --confidence {confidence} --minimum-hit-groups {min_hit_groups} {memory_mapping} --report {report} --output {assignments} "$@"

needs_database.label: Kraken2 database
needs_database.hint: Build a small one with Kraken2 build database, or download a ready-made one. Standard databases need 8 to 70 GB of memory.

tools.name: Bracken prepare database
tools.description: Gets a Kraken2 database ready for Bracken. Makes a new folder that links to your database and adds the files Bracken needs for one read length. Your database is not changed.

inputs.name: db
inputs.label: Kraken2 database
inputs.description: The Kraken2 database folder the reads were or will be classified against.

outputs.name: bracken_db
outputs.label: Prepared database
outputs.description: A folder that works as a Kraken2 database and as a Bracken database. Connect it to Kraken2 and Bracken.

params.label: Read length (bases)
params.description: The usual length of your reads. Run it again for another length.

params.label: Word size of the database
params.description: The word size the database was built with. The standard is 35.

tools.command: set -e; SRC=$(cd "{db}" && pwd); mkdir -p "{bracken_db}"; DST=$(cd "{bracken_db}" && pwd); if [ "$SRC" = "$DST" ]; then echo "Choose a new folder for the prepared database. It must not be the database itself." >&2; exit 1; fi; rm -f "$DST"/database*; for e in "$SRC"/*; do case "$(basename "$e")" in database*) ;; *) ln -sfn "$e" "$DST/$(basename "$e")";; esac; done; bracken-build -d "$DST" -t {threads} -k {kmer_length} -l {read_length}

needs_database.label: Kraken2 database
needs_database.hint: Use a Kraken2 database that still has its library folder. Ready-made indexes that include Bracken files do not need this step.

tools.name: Bracken
tools.description: Turns a Kraken2 summary into better abundance estimates. Reads that Kraken2 could only place on a genus are shared out over the species of that genus.

inputs.name: report
inputs.label: Kraken2 summary
inputs.description: The summary table written by Kraken2.

inputs.name: db
inputs.label: Prepared database
inputs.description: The database folder made by Bracken prepare database for the same read length, or a ready-made database that includes the Bracken files.

outputs.name: estimates
outputs.label: Abundance table
outputs.description: One line per species: reads Kraken2 gave it, reads added by Bracken, the estimate and its share of all reads (tab-separated).

outputs.name: new_report
outputs.label: Updated summary
outputs.description: The Kraken2 summary with the new numbers. MultiQC and Krona read it.

params.label: Read length (bases)
params.description: Must be a length the database was prepared for.

params.label: Group reads by
params.description: The level of the tree of life the estimates are made at.

params.label: Fewest reads to keep a group
params.description: Groups with fewer reads than this are left out before the estimate. 0 keeps all.

needs_database.label: Bracken database
needs_database.hint: Run Bracken prepare database on your Kraken2 database, or download an index that includes Bracken files for your read length.

tools.name: pod5 view
tools.description: Lists the reads in POD5 files as a table: read ID, channel, length in samples, start time and more. Use it to pick reads for pod5 filter or pod5 subset.

inputs.name: pods
inputs.label: POD5 files
inputs.description: A POD5 file holds the raw electrical signal of a Nanopore run. One or more files.

outputs.name: table
outputs.label: Read table
outputs.description: One line per read (tab-separated).

params.label: Columns to show
params.description: Optional. Comma-separated column names, for example read_id,channel,num_samples. Empty shows the standard columns.

tools.name: pod5 inspect
tools.description: Reports what a POD5 file holds: how many reads it has, how they are grouped into batches, and the version of the file format.

inputs.name: pod
inputs.label: POD5 file
inputs.description: A POD5 file holds the raw electrical signal of a Nanopore run.

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: Report
outputs.description: The summary as text.

tools.name: pod5 filter
tools.description: Copies only the reads you list into a new POD5 file. Use it to basecall or share a small part of a run.

inputs.name: pods
inputs.label: POD5 files
inputs.description: A POD5 file holds the raw electrical signal of a Nanopore run. One or more files holding the reads.

inputs.name: ids
inputs.label: Read IDs to keep
inputs.description: A text file with one read ID per line, for example made from the table of pod5 view.

outputs.name: filtered
outputs.label: Filtered file
outputs.description: A POD5 file with just the listed reads.

params.label: Skip IDs that are not in the files
params.description: Without this, pod5 filter stops when a listed read is not found.

tools.name: pod5 subset (split by column)
tools.description: Splits POD5 files into several files by a value in a table, for example one file per channel. The table can come from pod5 view or from a sequencing summary.

inputs.name: pods
inputs.label: POD5 files
inputs.description: A POD5 file holds the raw electrical signal of a Nanopore run. One or more files holding the reads.

inputs.name: table
inputs.label: Table of reads
inputs.description: A table with a read_id column and the column to split by, such as the output of pod5 view (tab-separated).

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Folder of files
outputs.description: One POD5 file per value, named after the value.

params.label: Split by column
params.description: The name of a column in the table. Use several, separated by spaces, to split by their combination.

params.label: Skip reads that are not in the files
params.description: Without this, pod5 subset stops when a table row names a read that is missing.

tools.name: pod5 merge
tools.description: Joins several POD5 files into one, for example the many files MinKNOW writes during a run.

inputs.name: pods
inputs.label: POD5 files
inputs.description: A POD5 file holds the raw electrical signal of a Nanopore run. Two or more files.

outputs.name: merged
outputs.label: Merged file
outputs.description: One POD5 file with the reads of all inputs.

params.label: Allow the same read twice if its signal is identical
params.description: Without this, pod5 merge stops when two files hold the same read ID.

tools.name: pod5 convert from FAST5
tools.description: Converts old FAST5 signal files to one POD5 file, the format Dorado reads.

inputs.name: fast5
inputs.label: FAST5 files
inputs.description: One or more FAST5 files (single-read or multi-read) from a Nanopore run.

outputs.name: converted
outputs.label: POD5 file
outputs.description: One POD5 file with every read of the FAST5 files.

tools.name: Dorado basecaller
tools.description: Turns the raw signal of a Nanopore run (POD5) into DNA sequence. Writes an unaligned BAM. Needs a graphics card or an Apple chip for anything but tests.

inputs.name: pod
inputs.label: POD5 file or folder
inputs.description: A POD5 file, or a folder of POD5 files. Convert old FAST5 files first.

outputs.name: calls
outputs.label: Basecalled reads
outputs.description: The reads with their sequence and quality, as an unaligned BAM.

params.label: Accuracy
params.description: Dorado picks the model that fits your flow cell and kit from the file. More accurate models are much slower.

option_labels.fast: Fast (for a quick look or tests)

params.label: Drop reads below this quality
params.description: Reads with an average quality score under this are not written. 10 is the usual cut. 0 keeps every read.

params.label: Run on
params.description: Auto uses the graphics card or Apple chip when there is one. The processor alone is very slow for real data.

option_labels.auto: Graphics card or Apple chip if available

tools.command: set -o pipefail; M="$HOME/.rustrunner/dorado-models"; mkdir -p "$M"; dorado basecaller {model} {pod} --models-directory "$M" --device {device} --min-qscore {min_qscore} --recursive > {calls}

needs_database.label: Basecalling model
needs_database.hint: Dorado downloads it on the first run (30 to 300 MB), so that run needs the internet.

tools.name: Dorado summary
tools.description: Makes a table with one line per read from a Dorado BAM: read ID, channel, length and quality. NanoPlot and pod5 subset read it.

inputs.name: calls
inputs.label: Basecalled reads
inputs.description: The BAM written by Dorado basecaller.

outputs.name: summary
outputs.label: Summary table
outputs.description: One line per read (tab-separated).

tools.name: UMI-tools extract
tools.description: Moves each read's UMI (unique molecular identifier) into its name and cuts it, and any spacer next to it, out of the sequence. Run it before aligning so duplicates can be removed later.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Reads
inputs.description: Sequencing reads in FASTQ format (plain or .gz). For a library with a 3' adapter, trim the adapter first.

outputs.name: extracted
outputs.label: Reads without the UMI
outputs.description: Reads with the UMI cut out. The UMI is now at the end of the read name, after an underscore.

outputs.name: log
outputs.label: Extraction log
outputs.description: How many reads were read and written. MultiQC reads it.

params.label: Where the UMI sits in the read
params.description: Most small-RNA and Ribo-seq kits put the UMI at the start of the read. Choose the 3' end only if your kit puts it at the end (after the adapter was trimmed).

params.label: UMI length (bases)
params.description: The number of bases of the UMI. 12 is the Diagenode D-Plex kit; check the manual of your kit.

params.label: Spacer bases to remove (next to the UMI)
params.description: Bases between the UMI and the insert that are not part of the sample and are removed too, for example a template-switching motif or a linker. 4 is the D-Plex kit; use 0 if there is none.

params.label: Your own pattern (advanced)
params.description: Leave empty to use the settings above. Otherwise a regular expression with a group umi_1 for the UMI and, optionally, discard_1, for example ^(?P<umi_1>.{8})(?P<discard_1>.{2})

tools.command: CUSTOM={custom_pattern}; if [ -n "$CUSTOM" ]; then PATTERN="$CUSTOM"; elif [ {umi_end} = 3prime ]; then PATTERN=".*(?P<discard_1>.{{spacer_length}})(?P<umi_1>.{{umi_length}})\$"; else PATTERN="^(?P<umi_1>.{{umi_length}})(?P<discard_1>.{{spacer_length}})"; fi; umi_tools extract --extract-method=regex --bc-pattern="$PATTERN" -I {reads} -S {extracted} -L {log}

tools.name: UMI-tools dedup
tools.description: Removes PCR duplicates: reads with the same start and UMI (allowing for UMI errors) count once. Needs a sorted BAM with its index, and read names that end in the UMI.

inputs.name: alignments
inputs.label: Sorted alignments
inputs.description: A coordinate-sorted BAM whose read names end in _UMI (made by UMI-tools extract before aligning).

inputs.name: index
inputs.label: BAM index
inputs.description: The .bai file next to the BAM (made by samtools index). It has to be called like the BAM with .bai added.

outputs.name: deduplicated
outputs.label: Alignments without duplicates
outputs.description: The BAM with one read kept for every group of duplicates.

outputs.name: log
outputs.label: Deduplication log
outputs.description: How many reads went in and came out. MultiQC reads it.

outputs.name: stats_dir
outputs.label: UMI statistics folder
outputs.description: Tables about UMI errors and counts per position (UMI-tools --output-stats), for your own checks. MultiQC needs only the log.

params.label: How to count UMIs

option_labels.unique: Unique: only identical UMIs are one molecule
option_labels.percentile: Percentile: ignores UMIs far rarer than the commonest
option_labels.cluster: Cluster: every UMI linked by a single error is one molecule
option_labels.adjacency: Adjacency: like cluster, with more careful choosing

params.description: Directional treats a rare UMI one error away from a much more common one as an error of the common one. It is the usual choice and the tool's default.

params.label: Compare reads by
params.description: Position: duplicates must start at the same place and share a UMI, as is standard for footprints. Whole transcript keeps one read per UMI and transcript and would erase the codon-level signal.

params.label: Also compare the read length
params.description: Reads with the same start and UMI but different lengths are different molecules (the 3' end of a footprint is where the enzyme cut), so they are kept. Untick to compare the start only.

params.label: UMI errors to allow
params.description: How many differing bases still count as the same UMI (not used by the Unique method). 1 is the tool default.

params.label: Random seed
params.description: Which read is kept from a group of duplicates is picked at random; the same seed gives the same result every time.

tools.command: BAM={alignments}; BAI={index}; if [ ! -s "$BAM.bai" ]; then echo "UMI-tools needs the BAM index next to the BAM, named $BAM.bai. The index given is $BAI." >&2; exit 1; fi; GROUP=""; if [ {group_by} = transcript ]; then GROUP="--per-gene --per-contig"; fi; umi_tools dedup -I "$BAM" -S {deduplicated} -L {log} --output-stats={stats_dir}dedup --method={method} --edit-distance-threshold={edit_distance} --random-seed={seed} {use_read_length} $GROUP

tools.name: Remove reads matching a database (bowtie2)
tools.description: Aligns reads to sequences you do not want (rRNA, tRNA, small RNAs, PhiX, a contaminant genome) and keeps the reads that do not match. Matches are counted in the log, not saved.

inputs.name: index
inputs.label: Database index
inputs.description: The index made with Bowtie2 build from the FASTA of the sequences to remove (connect it), or the prefix of one you built yourself.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Reads
inputs.description: Single-end reads in FASTQ format (plain or .gz).

outputs.name: unaligned
outputs.label: Reads that did not match
outputs.description: The reads that are left, as compressed FASTQ. Connect it to the next step.

outputs.name: log
outputs.label: Alignment summary
outputs.description: How many reads matched the database. MultiQC reads it; give each depletion step its own name.

params.label: How much of a read must match

option_labels.--local: Part of the read may match (local, finds the most)
option_labels.--end-to-end: The whole read must match (end to end)

params.description: Local removes a read when most of it matches, which also catches reads with leftover adapter or linker bases. End to end only removes reads that match along their whole length.

params.label: Sensitivity
params.description: Speed against thoroughness. Very sensitive is worth it here: a read that escapes removal is counted as sample.

params.label: Seed length (0 = keep the preset)
params.description: Length of the exact match (-L) bowtie2 starts from. 0 keeps the preset's (20); otherwise 4 to 31. A shorter seed such as 16 finds more distant matches in 25 to 35 base reads.

tools.command: set -o pipefail; set --; if [ {seed_length} -gt 0 ]; then set -- -L {seed_length}; fi; bowtie2 -p {threads} --reorder --{sensitivity} {alignment} "$@" -x {index} -U {reads} --un-gz {unaligned} -S /dev/null 2>&1 | tee {log} >&2

tools.name: STAR (Ribo-seq, transcriptome BAM)
tools.description: Aligns footprint reads to the genome and writes them in transcript coordinates, as riboWaltz needs. Defaults suit short footprints; reads that did not align stay in the BAM, marked unmapped.

inputs.name: index
inputs.label: Genome index folder (built with the gene annotation)
inputs.description: The folder made with STAR genome index (connect it). It must have been built with the gene annotation, otherwise STAR cannot write transcript coordinates.

inputs.name: reads
inputs.label: Reads
inputs.description: Single-end reads in FASTQ format (plain or .gz).

outputs.name: out_dir
outputs.label: Output folder
outputs.description: STAR writes the transcript BAM, its logs and, if asked, the genome BAM into this folder.

outputs.name: transcriptome_bam
outputs.label: Alignments in transcript coordinates
outputs.description: Aligned.toTranscriptome.out.bam: every read against the transcripts, in the order of the reads. Unaligned reads are in it too (flag 4); filter them with samtools view, then sort and index.

outputs.name: log
outputs.label: Mapping summary
outputs.description: STAR's mapping statistics. MultiQC reads it.

params.label: How much of a read must align

option_labels.EndToEnd: The whole read (end to end, recommended)
option_labels.Local: Part of the read (soft clipping allowed)

params.description: End to end keeps every aligned footprint: STAR leaves reads with soft clipping or indels out of the transcript BAM. Local loses the clipped ones from it.

params.label: Most mismatches per read
params.description: Reads with more mismatches are not aligned. 2 suits 25 to 35 base footprints; STAR's own default is 10, which is loose for short reads.

params.label: Most places a read may align to
params.description: 1 keeps only reads that align to one place, so every footprint has a single position (usual for Ribo-seq). Raise it to keep multi-mapping reads, which are then counted at each place.

params.label: Fewest matched bases per read
params.description: Reads with fewer matched bases are not aligned. Keep it at or below the shortest read you kept when trimming.

params.label: Genome-coordinate BAM

option_labels.BAM SortedByCoordinate: Also write it (for a genome browser)

params.description: The transcript BAM is what riboWaltz uses. A genome BAM is only needed to look at the alignments in a genome browser; it is written as Aligned.sortedByCoord.out.bam in the output folder.

tools.name: riboWaltz report
tools.description: Finds where the ribosome sits in each footprint (the P-site offset) and writes one HTML report: lengths, offsets, 3-nt periodicity, start and stop profiles, regions, codon usage, plus TSV tables.

inputs.name: bams
inputs.label: Alignments in transcript coordinates
inputs.description: One BAM per sample, aligned to transcripts (STAR Ribo-seq output after samtools view, sort and UMI-tools dedup). Connect several steps to compare samples.

inputs.name: annotation
inputs.label: Gene annotation
inputs.description: The GTF the STAR index was built with. Its transcript names must be the ones in the BAM, and each gene should have one transcript.

inputs.name: genome
inputs.label: Genome FASTA (optional)
inputs.description: The genome FASTA of the same release. Without it the report has no codon usage; everything else is still made.

outputs.name: report_dir
outputs.label: Report folder
outputs.description: The report and its tables.

outputs.name: report
outputs.label: HTML report
outputs.description: ribowaltz_report.html: one self-contained page you can open or send as it is.

outputs.name: offsets
outputs.label: P-site offsets table
outputs.description: psite_offsets.tsv: for every read length, where the P-site sits.

params.label: Shortest footprint to analyse
params.description: Reads shorter than this are left out of the offsets and the plots. Look at the read-length plot of your own data; 28 to 34 suits a library whose footprints peak at 31 to 32.

params.label: Longest footprint to analyse
params.description: Reads longer than this are left out. Must not be smaller than the shortest.

params.label: Read end used to find the offset
params.description: riboWaltz can place the P-site from either end of the footprint. Automatic picks the end that gives the clearer signal.

params.label: Bases around the start codon
params.description: A read is used to find the offset only if it extends at least this many bases on both sides of the start codon. riboWaltz's default is 6.
